name: Stirling Moss
context: TT winner at Dundrod in 1950, 1951 and 1955 — the first of his record seven Tourist Trophy wins came in Tommy Wisdom's XK120 in heavy rain, on the eve of his twenty-first birthday; the last came with John Fitch in Mercedes-Benz's 300 SLR.

name: Peter Whitehead
context: Won the 1950 Ulster Trophy in a Ferrari 125 — the first race meeting on the new circuit — setting fastest lap at 5:06.6. Defending the trophy in 1951, his Ferrari blew a piston on the warm-up.

appearances.result: Did not start — piston failure on the warm-up
Entered; photographed ahead of the works D-Type

name: Anthony Powys-Lybbe
context: Won the handicap contest at the opening August 1950 meeting in an Alfa Romeo P3.

name: Giuseppe Farina
context: The reigning Formula One World Champion won the 1951 Ulster Trophy in an Alfa Romeo 159 from pole position, setting a 4:44 lap record that stood for four years.

name: Piero Taruffi
context: Won the 1952 Ulster Trophy in a Vandervell-entered Ferrari 375.

name: Mike Hawthorn
context: Second in the 1952 Ulster Trophy in a Cooper-Bristol; won the 1953 Ulster Trophy and the 1954 TT scratch result; shared Jaguar's works D-Type with Titterington in 1955 and set the 4:42 lap record. He won the 1953 Ulster Trophy from pole, and in the 1955 TT set the sports-car lap record that stands forever at Dundrod: 4 minutes 42 seconds, 94.67 mph.

appearances.result: Retired late while leading the challenge to Mercedes
appearances.car: Works Jaguar D-Type, shared with Desmond Titterington

name: Juan Manuel Fangio
context: Appeared with Moss in the experimental V16 BRM at the 1952 Ulster Trophy; neither finished.

name: Peter Collins
context: Won the 1953 RAC TT with Pat Griffith in an Aston Martin DB3S.

name: Pat Griffith
context: Won the 1953 RAC TT with Peter Collins in an Aston Martin DB3S.

name: Maurice Trintignant
context: Shared the 1954 TT scratch and championship result with Mike Hawthorn in a Ferrari 750 Monza.

name: Gérard Laureau
context: With Paul Armagnac, took the 1954 Tourist Trophy under the handicap classification in a small DB-Panhard.

name: Paul Armagnac
context: With Gérard Laureau, took the 1954 Tourist Trophy under the handicap classification in a small DB-Panhard.

name: Desmond Titterington
context: Local driver from Holywood. Fastest finisher in the 1955 Ulster Trophy handicap, and shared the factory Jaguar D-Type with Hawthorn in the 1955 TT. Within a year of his Ulster Trophy win he was racing in Grand Prix company.

appearances.result: Retired late while leading the challenge to Mercedes
appearances.car: Works Jaguar D-Type, shared with Mike Hawthorn

name: Bill Smith
context: Won the handicap Champion Trophy at the May 1955 Ulster Trophy meeting in a Jaguar C-Type.

name: John Fitch
context: Shared Moss's winning Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR in the 1955 TT.

name: Jim Mayers
context: Died in the multi-car crash at Deer's Leap on the second lap of the 1955 TT.

name: William Smith
context: Died in the multi-car crash at Deer's Leap on the second lap of the 1955 TT.

name: Richard Mainwaring
context: Died when his Elva crashed at Tornagrough during the 1955 TT.

name: Eric Winterbottom
context: Died in a first-lap crash at the 1951 Tourist Trophy.

name: Raymond Mays
context: Pictured with the BRM team around the V16 at the 1952 Ulster Trophy.

name: Alfred Neubauer
context: Mercedes team manager, pictured with Stirling Moss at Dundrod in 1955.

name: Bob Gerard
context: Second in the opening 1950 Ulster Trophy, bringing his pre-war ERA home sixteen seconds behind Whitehead's Ferrari.

name: Bobby Baird
context: Belfast newspaper proprietor — his family founded the Belfast Telegraph — and Ulster's own Ferrari entrant. He crashed his MG-based special at the very first 1950 meeting, built the Maserati-engined Baird-Griffon, and took third in the 1953 Ulster Trophy in a Ferrari 500. He was killed at Snetterton in July 1953; the 1953 TT programme carried the Ulster Automobile Club's tribute to him.

name: Reg Parnell
context: Rated the top British driver of the day, he split the works Alfa Romeos to finish second to Farina in the 1951 Ulster Trophy, and appears in the archive in the Thinwall Special Ferrari.

name: Joe Kelly
context: Irish privateer in his Alta: fourth in the first Ulster Trophy of 1950 and third behind Taruffi and Hawthorn in 1952.

name: Sydney Allard
context: Founder of the Allard marque, he brought the Steyr-engined Allard special to the opening 1950 Ulster Trophy, retiring with a gasket failure after nine laps.

name: Prince Bira
context: The Siamese prince entered the 1952 Ulster Trophy with his 4.5-litre OSCA-engined car — photographed in the Dundrod pits that June.

name: Tony Rolt
context: Le Mans winner of 1953 for Jaguar, photographed in a C-Type at Dundrod the same season — the TT in which the Jaguars were slowed by transmission trouble.

name: Lance Macklin
context: Austin-Healey works driver, photographed sharing a 100S with John Dalton in the 1955 Tourist Trophy.

name: Louis Rosier
context: The French veteran and 1950 Le Mans winner brought his 4.5-litre Ferrari to the 1951 Ulster Trophy, and appears in the 1952 paddock photographs.

name: Peter Walker
context: Jaguar's other C-Type man of 1951: second in that year's Tourist Trophy behind his young team-mate Moss.

name: Ken Wharton
context: Second in the 1953 Ulster Trophy final, chasing Hawthorn's Ferrari in a Cooper-Bristol.

name: Cuth Harrison
context: Third in the opening 1950 Ulster Trophy in his pre-war ERA.

name: Brian Shawe-Taylor
context: Took pole position for the very first race on the new circuit in his ERA, and stood on the 1951 Ulster Trophy podium behind Farina and Parnell.

appearances.result: Pole position (finishing position not recorded in the register)
